bull.b: Positive operating cash flow and higher adjusted EBITDA indicate the core mine can fund ongoing operations. This provides a durable base for sustaining investment, although future cash generation still depends on restoring production volumes.

The capacity expansion can increase processing potential and improve fixed-cost absorption over time. If commissioning proceeds as planned, greater throughput should support production growth and help normalize unit costs.

Revenue and gross margin remained substantial despite materially lower output, demonstrating operating resilience and pricing leverage. This supports the viability of the existing mine while expansion and development projects progress.

bear.b: Negative equity weakens financial flexibility and makes balance-sheet-based returns difficult to interpret. Noncash SPAC and warrant accounting also distorts reported earnings, reducing confidence in the quality and stability of reported results.

The production shortfall reduced fixed-cost absorption and increased cash costs per ounce, pressuring mine economics. A durable recovery requires successful ore-body transition and development execution, not only stronger gold prices.

The large capital requirement is substantial relative to current cash generation and creates funding, dilution, and execution risk. Uncertain financing could delay project timelines or limit the company’s ability to capture planned growth.
